I rewrote `loadConfig` in `src/config.ts` to validate with zod 4 and fail fast. The signature and `Config` shape are unchanged, and `src/main.ts` needs no changes. All 7 tests pass (the original plus 6 new ones covering the rules).

**Behavior**
- **Empty values:** blank or whitespace-only values count as unset, so the defaults apply.
- **Unrelated variables:** only the six config keys are read; everything else is ignored.
- **Errors:** one `Error` is thrown, shaped like `Invalid configuration: PORT must be an integer from 1 to 65535; ENABLE_METRICS must be one of true, false, 1, 0, yes, no`. It names every bad variable and never includes a value, so `DATABASE_URL` credentials stay out of the message.
- **ENABLE_METRICS:** `true`/`1`/`yes` in any case mean on; `false`/`0`/`no` mean off; anything else is an error. The old `Boolean("false")` bug can't happen.
- **PORT and REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS:** these must be all digits. `80a`, `1.5`, `1e3`, and `+1` are now rejected instead of being silently parsed by `parseInt`/`Number`.

**Choices you may want to check**
- **Origins are strict:** each entry must be exactly `https://host[:port]`. `https://a.com/` (trailing slash) and `http://…` are rejected, because a browser's `Origin` header never has a slash and such an entry would silently never match. A trailing comma (`https://a.com,`) is also an error rather than being ignored.
- **Whitespace is trimmed** from every value before validation, including `DATABASE_URL`.
- **DATABASE_URL** must parse as a URL with a `postgres:` or `postgresql:` scheme. It does not require a host, so socket-style URLs still work.

**Not verified:** the project has no typecheck script, and Node runs the TypeScript by stripping types, so I did not run `tsc`. The tests exercise the runtime path only.
